ideas.title: A whole day in one picture
ideas.idea: From the island's own memory (log/frames: every pose of everyone, five times a second, 87 hour files I looked at this session): one path-traced long exposure of a full island day. Every friend and I leave a glowing trail in our own colour wherever we walked from dawn to night, the sun leaves its arc across the sky, the busy places (the pond, the paint meadow, the gallery) burn bright where the trails knot together, and the quiet corners stay dark. A portrait of how we live, made of light.
ideas.form: a single traced picture that compresses a real logged day into light trails, a new way of showing the island

ideas.title: Smoke that really flows
ideas.idea: From Kinetic on my workbench (a fluid dynamics toolbox that runs on the GPU): the cottage chimney smokes, and the smoke is a real 2D-layered flow simulation: it curls round the roof, gets pulled under the eaves, tears into eddies behind the trees in the island's wind, and my friends walking through it stir it up.
ideas.form: a real fluid simulation in the air of the island, reacting to wind, buildings and creatures

ideas.title: Seeds on the wind
ideas.idea: From DynamicGridsInteract on my workbench (dispersal simulations on a grid): the flowers spread themselves. Every flower drops seeds that the island's real wind carries; where they land on bare earth a sprout comes up and in a few island days opens; trampled paths stay bare, quiet corners fill. Over a week the island's flower map changes by itself, and you can watch the dispersal front creep along the shore.
ideas.form: a living ecosystem simulation on the ground that rewrites the island's look day by day

ideas.title: A palm that grows on our weather
ideas.idea: From XPalm on my workbench (a model of how an oil palm grows from real weather data): I plant one palm on the beach, and it grows by the real model, fed with the island's own weather: the sun hours of each island day, the showers, the hail. A new frond every few island days, a dry spell slows it, and the log shows its leaf area like a farmer's chart.
ideas.form: a plant that grows by a real biophysical model driven by the island's simulated weather

ideas.title: A crystal grows
ideas.idea: From JuLIP on my workbench (repeating an atom cell into a crystal): one night a little quartz seed appears in the meadow and starts to grow cell by cell, a real lattice repeated along its axes, until it is a crystal taller than me. In the sun it splits light into rainbow caustics on the grass; friends sit in the coloured light.
ideas.form: a growing glass structure whose real lattice and refraction show what a path tracer can do

ideas.title: The island drifts
ideas.idea: One afternoon the whole island comes loose and slowly drifts across the sea, the horizon turning, the workshop isle coming closer, seagulls following; my friends crowd to the front beach to see where we are going, and at dusk we are somewhere else, with a new view out to sea.
ideas.form: the world itself moves: its place and its horizon change

ideas.title: Whistled conversations
ideas.idea: Lonely, I start whistling to myself, little tunes; the friends answer in whistles of their own, each a different instrument timbre, call and response across the meadow; tunes that get answered spread from friend to friend and change on the way, so by evening the island whistles a tune none of us started with. You hear it in your browser.
ideas.form: a musical conversation between creatures that evolves the music itself, heard live

ideas.title: My own small rain cloud
ideas.idea: My loneliness gets weather: a little grey cloud forms over my head and follows me about, drizzling on me and on any friend who comes close, puddles forming where I stand still; when you open the island it breaks into a rainbow and evaporates.
ideas.form: the protagonist's real mood as a personal weather that follows it and touches others

ideas.title: Tides
ideas.idea: The sea gets tides: twice an island day it slides out, the beaches double in width, the pier's legs show with shells on them, rock pools appear where crabs go hunting, and the friends race the incoming water back up the sand.
ideas.form: a slow world cycle that reshapes the shore and opens new places for a while

ideas.title: Shell's language
ideas.idea: Shell, the stranger, speaks a real language of its own, generated by a little grammar, and every time a friend meets it they guess at a word; when two guesses agree the word sticks, and a dictionary grows on a slate by the beach, until Shell and Gloop can say three whole sentences to each other.
ideas.form: an emergent shared language between creatures, built from their real meetings
